L219: ### Who should complete the CST Diploma?
L220: 
L221: This program might be for you if:
L222: 
L223:   * You’re interested in software development
L224:   * You enjoy problem-solving, often in teams
L225:   * You’re enthusiastic about using technology, computers, and software systems to make things better
L226:   * You’re ready to apply yourself to prepare for a career in the evolving and rapidly expanding Computing and IT sector
L227: If any of these sound like you, please check the cite63†Entrance Requirements to ensure you can apply and start your new IT career!
L228: ### What Computer Systems Technology grads can do?
L229: 
L230: By earning your BCIT Diploma, you’ll be honing your IT skills and gaining knowledge of various industry-recognized technologies, preparing you for positions in multiple industries and locations.
L231: 
L232: As a CST graduate, you’ll be able to:
L233:   * Participate in all aspects of software development and maintenance
L234:   * Contribute and communicate effectively as a member of software project teams
L235:   * Design and code with widely-used programming languages and scripting tools, which include JavaScript, Python, Java, C, and C++
L236:   * Develop and maintain complex software systems that integrate scalable components, such as Cloud Computing
L237:   * Apply logical, critical, and creative thinking to effectively solve Computing and IT-related problems
L238:   * Synthesize solutions to novel problems using various approaches, including Artificial Intelligence (AI)
L239:   * Work productively and meet deadlines in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment
L240:   * Independently learn and adopt new tools, current technologies and methods to stay industry-ready.
L241:   * Engage with a well-established alumni community of CST Grads in industry
L242: And you also have the option to continue your education with various bachelor’s degree programs, including the cite91†Bachelor of Science in Applied Computer Science . Learn more about the opportunities awaiting you on the cite68†Graduating and Jobs page .

L247: The Computer Systems Technology program is offered at both the Burnaby and Downtown campuses. Accepted applicants will be assigned to either the Burnaby or Downtown Campus as part of their admission offer.
L248: ### Transfer credit
L249: 
L250: Equivalent courses from BCIT and other institutions may be transferable to the Computer Systems Technology program based on the recommendations of the instructor and the program head.
L251: 
L252: To be considered for course credit, students must:
L253:   * Be accepted into the diploma program.
L254:   * Have earned a minimum of 60% final grade in the equivalent course or courses.
L255:   * Have completed the courses within an acceptable recency of five years.
L256:   * Be able to demonstrate coverage of course learning outcomes in the equivalent course or courses.
L257: BCIT policy allows only a maximum of 50 percent of a credential’s credits to be awarded through previously earned credits. If you have taken an equivalent course and meet the above requirements, apply for transfer credit by submitting a cite92†Course Credit Exemption form [PDF] .

L278: ### Conditions
L279: 
L280: The Computer Systems Technology program is offered at both the Burnaby and Downtown campuses. Accepted applicants will be assigned to either the Burnaby or Downtown Campus as part of their admission offer.
L281: 
L282: You may be eligible to apply to an advanced level of the program through either cite95†re-admission or cite96†direct entry . Please note that applications are considered based on:
L283:   * Complete applications: you must show proof that you have completed (or are registered in) all requirements to be considered.
L284:   * Competitive entry: if the number of applicants exceeds available seats, BCIT will accept those deemed to have the best opportunity for success.
L285:   * Seat availability: confirmation may not be available until approximately one week before the term begins.
L286: Note: The Registrar's Office is the official authority on admission and entrance requirements and has the final say on whether or not you meet all entrance requirements for this program. You are responsible for submitting sufficient documentation to BCIT Admissions to be assessed.
L287: ### Direct entry
L288: 
L289: If you are new to the program but have completed an equivalent part of it at BCIT or elsewhere and want to apply to an advanced level, you can apply for direct entry to level 2 or 3. Note that if you enter the program via direct entry, you are not eligible to apply for the Co-op program.

L224: Course guides provide direction of learning in preparation, in course activities and reflection of the content. The instructor acts as facilitator and expert to promote an environment conducive for learning through activities such as guided discussion, debate, audio-visual presentation, group activities, skill building exercises and simulation. Some courses may be offered in a blended delivery mode.
L225: Level one provides the foundation for the development of nursing practice and introduces the learner to the healthy adult.
L226: 
L227: Level two explores the older adult and concepts related to aging and chronic illness in various settings.
L228: 
L229: Level three examines a continuum of care in the community health setting and applies concepts from level one, two and three in the management of stable clients across the lifespan.
L230: Level four integrates knowledge from previous levels and examines concepts related to the care of the medical/surgical client.
L231: 
L232: Each level is supported by a Consolidated Practice Experience (CPE) which reinforces the learning that has taken place within each level.
L233: 
L234: Eligibility to enter the Consolidated Practice Experience at the end of each level is dependent upon the successful completion of all of the other courses within that level.
L235: Each level must be successfully completed before the next one can be attempted.
L236:

L242: ## Admission requirements
L243: ### Program-specific
L244: 
L245: Core minimum standards for admission requirements, including English as an Additional Language standard have been established by the Provincial Practical Nursing Program Curriculum. VCC admission requirements for this program are in addition to those provincial expectations. All of these requirements must be met.
L246: 
L247:   * BC Grade 12 or equivalent
L248:   * English Studies 12 with a minimum 'B' grade, or equivalent
L249:   * Foundations of Math 11 with a minimum 'C' grade, or equivalent
L250:   * BIOL 1602 Human Anatomy and Physiology with a minimum grade of 68% or equivalent within the last 3 years
L251: 
L252:   * cite127†English Language Proficiency as specified for the Practical Nursing or Access to Practical Nursing programs
L253: 
L254: Internationally Trained Nurses:
L255: 
L256:   * Students with transcripts from outside of Canada may be required to submit a comprehensive evaluation form from an cite128†educational credential assessment service provider†www.canada.ca .
L257: 
L258: 
L259: Upon Acceptance into the program:
L260:   * Criminal Record Check (CRC):
L261: 
L262: Students in this program are required to complete a CRC. The CRC must be completed according to cite129†VCC's Criminal Record Check instructions . Students whose CRC results indicate they pose a risk to vulnerable populations will not be able to complete the requirements of the program (e.g. practicums) or graduate.
L263: 
L264:   * Valid cite130†CPR-BLS certification :
L265: 
L266: Certificate must remain valid throughout the program.
L267: 
L268:   * TB skin test:
L269: Students must submit a negative tuberculosis (TB) skin test or chest X-ray dated a maximum of six months prior to the program start date. An additional TB test is required after each potential exposure to TB and/or travel to areas with a known prevalence of TB.
L270: 
L271:   * Immunization Record:
L272: A cite131†School of Health Sciences Student Immunization Record must be completed. Students may be declined placement in a clinical or practicum site if a completed immunization record is not provided.
L273: 
L274:   * N95 mask:
L275: Regulations stipulate that a properly fitted respiratory mask must be used when providing care to patients with suspected, known, or probable cases of acute respiratory infections. The respiratory mask must be a N95 respirator that is individually fitted by a trained and certified person. This individual mask fitting should be done just prior to beginning your program and is good for one year and must be performed annually.
L276: The original certificate must be presented to your program during the first week of classes.

L220: ### Entrance requirements
L221: 
L222: Competitive Entry: Three-step process
L223: 
L224: Meeting the minimum entrance requirements does not guarantee admission. Admission is competitive, and qualified applicants are assessed and ranked based on the department’s competitive selection criteria. Offers of admission are made to the most competitive applicants based on the available seats for each intake.
L225: When the number of qualified applicants exceeds the available seats, the program may establish a waitlist. Waitlisted applicants who are not admitted will be invited to have their application considered for the following intake. Future-intake consideration does not guarantee admission.
L226: 
L227: Step 1: Meet the following entrance requirements
L228: 
L229:   * English language proficiency: cite87†Category 2 – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent
L230:   * Math: one of the following or equivalent:
L231:     * Pre-Calculus 11 (73%) or 12 (67%) or
L232:     * Foundations of Math 11 (73%) or 12 (73%) or
L233:     * cite88†MATH 0007 – Technical Mathematics Introduction (73%)
L234: 
L235:   * Chemistry 11 (73%) or equivalent
L236:   * Academic Foundations: 18.0 post-secondary credits with a minimum of 67% in each of the following courses:
L237:     * cite89†ENGL 1177 – Academic Writing or equivalent* (3.0 credits)
L238: Note: ENGL 1177 may also be used to satisfy the English language proficiency.
L239:     * cite90†BHSC 1200 – Human Anatomy and Physiology or equivalent*, completed within the past three years (6.0 credits)
L240:     * cite91†PSYC 1101 – Introductory Psychology 1 or equivalent* (3.0 credits)
L241:     * cite92†General Education [PDF] electives at a 100-level minimum in at least two different academic disciplines (6.0 credits)
L242: * View acceptable cite93†equivalent courses [PDF] L243: 
L244: Applicants must submit final grades for the listed Academic Foundations courses by the application deadline. In-progress courses are not accepted for this program.
L245: 
L246:   * Complete the following form for submission with your online application:
L247:     * cite94†Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire [PDF] : This form will be used with other entrance requirements in the competitive selection for the program.
L248: Applicants who have completed post-secondary studies outside of Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or New Zealand will require a comprehensive evaluation of their credentials by the cite95†International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES) . Credential evaluation reports from other cite96†Canadian services†www.cicic.ca may be considered. These reports must include course-by-course evaluations and GPA calculations.

L253: Applicants who meet the minimum entrance requirements will be assessed and ranked competitively. Admission decisions are based on academic achievement and the assessment of the Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire.

L255: Preference will be given to applicants who demonstrate:

L257:   * Additional post-secondary education
L258:   * Exposure to healthcare environments, patient care, or community service through employment, volunteer activities, or other experiences
L259:   * Relevant knowledge, skills, experiences, and attributes aligned with the nursing profession

L261: Preference may also be given to applicants who were previously waitlisted and highly ranked.

L146: ## April 23, 2026
L147: 
L148: BC Provincial Nominee Program Priorities and Program Updates
L149: The BC Provincial Nominee Program (BC PNP) delivers strong economic outcomes and has been updated to support B.C.’s cite96†Look West strategy†www2.gov.bc.ca , with a renewed focus on attracting top talent and addressing critical labour market needs. These updates are guided by three core objectives:
L150: (1) Care—strengthening healthcare and other services within the care economy;
L151: (2) Build—supporting the delivery of infrastructure and major projects; and
L152: (3) Innovate—advancing innovation to help drive long term economic growth.
L153: These changes will benefit all regions of B.C., with at least 35% of all nominations anticipated to be for candidates working in communities outside Metro Vancouver.
L154: Care
L155: The BC PNP will prioritize skilled workers that support public services and community well-being. This includes cite97†36 in-demand occupations in healthcare, education, childcare, and veterinary care.
L156: The BC PNP Health Authority stream will continue to nominate qualified healthcare professionals who work in the public sector directly delivering healthcare services. The program will also nominate select healthcare occupations working in the broader health sector.
L157: Certified early childhood educators, veterinarians and veterinary technologists who are working toward Canadian certification will be prioritized.
L158: The BC PNP will also leverage cite98†additional federal allocations that are available to support francophone recruitment†www.canada.ca by prioritizing French speaking teachers working for the province’s public K-12 school system.
L159: Temporary time-limited initiative
L160: The BC PNP will deliver a time-limited, one-time initiative to retain up to 250 workers already working for a health authority in a cleaning or security role in a rural or remote community who meet program criteria. This initiative will open in June 2026 to registrations using the BC PNP’s expression of interest system. More information will be provided before intake opens.

L101: ## Pathway to permanent residency as a worker
L102: 
L103: The BC Provincial Nominee Program (BC PNP) offers a pathway to permanent residency for workers with the experience and qualifications needed in British Columbia. Through Skills Immigration, workers who meet specific eligibility criteria based on their job offer can choose to apply to the Skilled Worker or Health Authority stream.
L104: To view eligibility and requirements for the Temporary Rural / Remote Health Support initiative, see the cite91†Skills Immigration Program Guide .
L105: 
L106: Applicants who are successfully nominated by the BC PNP through one of its immigration streams can apply for permanent residence in Canada.
L107: 
L108: Please note: the program prioritizes workers who meet the labour market and economic development needs of B.C. To learn more, please see the BC PNP's cite92†selection of workers list .
